overview: This report covers 31 unseen announcements: 8 HIGH PRIORITY, 14 RELATED / POSSIBLY INTERESTING, and 9 LOW PRIORITY. Central themes include equilibrium and maximal-entropy measures, entropy variation on negatively curved surfaces, fractal transference and dimensions of attractors and graphs, and approximation under torus group actions. paper.title: Computer-assisted proofs of periodic solutions of state-dependent delay equations beyond perturbative regimes
paper.abstract: Rigorous existence results for periodic solutions of state-dependent delay differential equations (SDDEs) are scarce outside perturbative regimes, where the equation is close to an ordinary or constant-delay differential equation. We develop a computer-assisted framework that proves the existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs directly. The numerical approximation is a trigonometric polynomial, and a true periodic solution nearby is obtained by a Newton--Kantorovich argument in the space of $C^1$ periodic functions. The main difficulty lies in the terms in which the solution is evaluated at a time that itself depends on the solution. We obtain rigorous enclosures of their Fourier coefficients by adapting validated discrete Fourier transform techniques for analytic nonlinearities. We apply the framework to three representative examples of increasing complexity: a periodically forced toy model, an autonomous scalar equation with two state-dependent delays, and a threshold-type delay model from operon dynamics in gene regulation. To our knowledge, these are the first computer-assisted proofs of existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs outside perturbative regimes. This opens the way to computer-assisted proofs for SDDEs more broadly. All computer-assisted proofs, including the requisite codes and the approximate objects, are accessible on GitHub at \cite{code_proof}.

analysis.relevance_note: Computer-assisted existence of delay-equation periodic solutions is central, without a stated connection to the strongest profile themes.

paper.title: Boundary and Interior of Root Sets of Power Series
paper.abstract: In this paper we study the set $\mathcal{M}_M$ of roots of power series with coefficients in $\{0, \pm 1, ..., \pm M \}$ and constant coefficient $1$. We prove that every nonreal root in the unit disk of a polynomial of this form is an interior point of $\mathcal{M}_M$. Moreover we establish a dimension formula and show the corresponding Hausdorff measure is finite and positive for a family of attractors parameterized by boundary parameters $\lambda \in \partial \mathcal{M}_M \setminus \mathbb{R}$. Finally we show that $\partial \mathcal{M}_M$ has Lebesgue measure zero.

analysis.tldr: The authors study interiors and boundaries of root sets of bounded-integer-coefficient power series and establish a dimension formula for a family of attractors.

analysis.main_result: Every nonreal root in the unit disk of a polynomial of the prescribed form is an interior point of the corresponding power-series root set. For attractors parameterized by nonreal boundary parameters, the authors establish a dimension formula and finite positive corresponding Hausdorff measure; the formula is not specified in the abstract. The boundary of the root set has Lebesgue measure zero.

paper.title: Complete Expanding Interval Maps are Mixing
paper.abstract: We give a new and elementary\footnote{That is: without functional analysis.} proof that certain smooth, complete, expanding maps from the interval to itself are mixing.

paper.title: Integer points for iterated Weierstrass elliptic functions
paper.abstract: Iterated Weierstrass P functions exhibit relationships between period lattices and the dynamics. We connect the dynamical properties to the occurrence of integer and rational points on associated real elliptic curves. Defining a complex number z to be an integer point if both P(z) and P'(z) are integers, we restrict to P when the lattice is real and its invariants g2 and g3 are integers. We study when an integer point lies in the Fatou set of P and when it lies in the Julia set, and if there is any dynamical significance to this. Applying established results on integer solutions to cubic Diophantine equations to the dynamical properties of iterated elliptic P functions, we show integer points at poles of P lie in the Julia set. Integer points can also occur in the Fatou set of P.

analysis.relevance_note: The Fatou/Julia classification gives a complex-dynamics connection, although dimension and entropy are not stated.
analysis.tldr: For Weierstrass elliptic functions associated with real lattices and integer invariants, the authors connect integer points on associated elliptic curves with Fatou and Julia dynamics.
analysis.problem: Determine dynamical significance and Fatou/Julia membership of integer points, defined by integral values of the elliptic function and its derivative.
analysis.main_result: Under the stated real-lattice and integer-invariant restrictions, the abstract reports that integer points at poles of the elliptic function lie in its Julia set, while integer points can also occur in its Fatou set. Further criteria are not specified in the abstract.
methods: Established results on integer solutions to cubic Diophantine equations.
analysis.context: Iteration of Weierstrass elliptic functions and arithmetic of real elliptic curves.

paper.title: Variations of the harmonic entropy and linear drift on negatively curved surfaces
paper.abstract: For closed negatively curved surfaces, we obtain formulas for the derivatives of the harmonic entropy of its geodesic flow and the linear drift of its Brownian motion along conformal deformations. We deduce that the harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow of a closed surface of non-constant negative curvature (resp. linear drift of the Brownian motion on its universal cover) is strictly decreasing (resp. increasing) along the normalized Ricci flow. We also prove that any hyperbolic metric on a surface admits a neighborhood in the space of conformal negatively curved metrics in which the linear drift is greater or equal to the Liouville entropy, with equality if and only if the metric is hyperbolic.

analysis.relevance_note: Variation of harmonic entropy is directly aligned with entropy theory.
analysis.tldr: The authors derive conformal variation formulas for harmonic entropy and Brownian linear drift on closed negatively curved surfaces and obtain monotonicity along normalized Ricci flow.
analysis.problem: Understand how harmonic entropy and linear drift vary under conformal deformations and compare drift with Liouville entropy near hyperbolic metrics.
analysis.main_result: For closed surfaces of nonconstant negative curvature, harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow strictly decreases and Brownian linear drift on the universal cover strictly increases along normalized Ricci flow. Every hyperbolic surface metric has a neighborhood among conformal negatively curved metrics where drift is at least Liouville entropy, with equality exactly for hyperbolic metrics. The derivative formulas themselves are not specified in the abstract.
methods: Derivative formulas along conformal deformations.
analysis.context: Entropy of geodesic flows, Brownian motion and negatively curved geometry.

paper.abstract: We expand our discussion of the almost stability theorem of Dicks and Dunwoody in the context of probability measure preserving equivalence relations.

paper.title: A Homological Approach to Dynamics
paper.abstract: This note describes a novel approach to systematically characterize dynamics based on finite information. We present an algebraic framework for dynamics from which it is possible to deduce more traditional descriptors associated with the qualitative structures of the geometric theory of dynamical systems. The purpose of this paper is to indicate how this approach can be used to obtain interpretable characterizations of dynamics that are robust with respect to perturbations, in the context of models of multiscale and data-driven systems.

analysis.relevance_note: A homological and algebraic description of qualitative dynamics has a plausible connection to topological dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors present an algebraic framework for characterizing dynamics from finite information, aimed at interpretable descriptions robust under perturbation.

analysis.main_result: The note describes a framework from which traditional geometric descriptors of dynamics can be deduced and indicates its use for perturbation-robust characterizations. Specific theorem hypotheses are not specified in the abstract.

paper.title: Periodic Solutions and Exponential Attractivity in Hopfield-Type Neural Networks with Generalized Piecewise Constant Arguments: Impulsive and Nonimpulsive Cases
paper.abstract: We investigate an impulsive Hopfield-type neural network with a generalized piecewise constant argument, including the nonimpulsive case in which all jump terms vanish. The piecewise constant argument is given by $\gamma(t)=\zeta_k$ on each interval $[t_k,t_{k+1})$, where $t_k\leq\zeta_k\leq t_{k+1}$, $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$. Depending on the position of $\zeta_k$, the argument may be advanced, retarded, or of mixed type. By representing periodic solutions through a Green function and applying a fixed-point argument, we obtain explicit and verifiable sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an $\omega$-periodic solution. We then use a Gronwall-type estimate, together with period averages, to prove that this solution is globally exponentially attractive. These conditions can be checked directly from the system parameters, without requiring explicit knowledge of the periodic solution. In the course of the analysis, we also revisit and correct some estimates presented by Pinto et al. \cite{Pinto_ejqtde}. The case $\zeta_k=t_k$ reduces to their setting, whereas our results cover the more general choice of $\zeta_k$ within each interval. We also present examples illustrating different types of piecewise constant arguments.

analysis.relevance_note: Periodic-solution existence and exponential attractivity in a neural-network delay model are central, without the profile themes stated.

paper.title: Geometric structures, orbit closures and invariant measures in moduli spaces
paper.abstract: Building on the seminal work of Eskin, Mirzakhani and Mohammadi in the context of dynamics on moduli spaces, we introduce linear loci and linear measures to provide a relatively basic description of orbit closures and invariant measures in strata of translation surfaces. We use this to discuss geometrical properties of orbit closures and invariant measures from the perspective of geometric structures.

analysis.tldr: The authors introduce linear loci and linear measures to describe orbit closures and invariant measures in strata of translation surfaces.

analysis.context: Dynamics on moduli spaces of translation surfaces.

paper.title: Fractal transference principle for conformal iterated function systems
paper.abstract: We establish a complex one-dimensional fractal transference principle connecting density combinatorics with the fractal geometry of complex continued fractions. Our framework applies to a broad class of conformal iterated function systems indexed by lattice points, including those associated with the Hurwitz continued fraction, and transfers positive-density combinatorial patterns to digit sets while preserving the maximal Hausdorff dimension. As applications, we obtain fractal counterparts of the multidimensional and polynomial Szemer\'edi theorems, as well as their relativized versions yielding a counterpart of the multidimensional Green--Tao theorem.

analysis.relevance_note: Conformal iterated function systems and preservation of maximal Hausdorff dimension directly match the fractal profile.
analysis.tldr: A complex one-dimensional fractal transference principle transfers positive-density combinatorial patterns to continued-fraction digit sets while preserving maximal Hausdorff dimension.
analysis.problem: Connect density combinatorics with the fractal geometry of complex continued fractions for conformal iterated function systems indexed by lattice points.
analysis.main_result: The framework applies to a broad class of these systems, including Hurwitz continued fractions. Applications give fractal counterparts of multidimensional and polynomial Szemerédi theorems and relativized versions yielding a counterpart of the multidimensional Green–Tao theorem.
methods: A fractal transference principle for lattice-indexed conformal iterated function systems.
analysis.context: Fractal geometry, complex continued fractions and density combinatorics.

paper.title: Non-convergence in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics: The bounded influence model
paper.abstract: In a recent preprint, we found counterexamples to a number of auxiliary conjectures in a 2012 paper of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo, concerning convergence in two fundamental models of heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics, the synchronized bounded confidence (SBC) and synchronized bounded influence (SBI) models. Building on our work, Etesami and Touri presented an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBC dynamics, resolving the main conjecture from the 2012 paper in that case. Here we complete this project by presenting an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBI dynamics. The example was found with the help of AI.

analysis.relevance_note: The nonconvergent opinion-dynamics example has no stated central connection to the entropy, fractal, symbolic or group-action profile.

paper.title: The K-property of equilibrium states for systems with non-uniform structure
paper.abstract: In this paper, we develop a general criterion for the K-property of equilibrium states within the Climenhaga-Thompson framework. Under suitable pressure-gap and non-uniform expansiveness assumptions, we show that the unique equilibrium state has the K-property, provided that the good collection of orbit segments satisfies an appropriate non-uniform specification property, as well as an appropriate non-uniform distortion control property for the potential function. These results do not require any additional lambda-decomposition structure and apply to a wide range of systems, including those with non-trivial central directions, such as the frame flow over closed rank-one manifolds with bunched nonpositive curvature. Moreover, we also construct several counterexamples to demonstrate that generally the assumptions in our criteria cannot be weakened while keeping the K-property.

analysis.relevance_note: Equilibrium states, pressure gaps and non-uniform specification are central profile topics.
analysis.tldr: The authors give a criterion for the K-property of equilibrium states in the Climenhaga–Thompson framework, without an additional lambda-decomposition structure.
analysis.problem: Identify conditions ensuring the K-property for the unique equilibrium state of a system with non-uniform structure.
analysis.main_result: The criterion assumes suitable pressure gaps and non-uniform expansiveness, and appropriate non-uniform specification of good orbit segments and non-uniform distortion control of the potential. Precise versions of these conditions are not specified in the abstract. Applications include frame flows over closed rank-one manifolds with bunched nonpositive curvature, and counterexamples show that the assumptions generally cannot be weakened while retaining the K-property.
methods: The Climenhaga–Thompson framework; counterexample constructions.
analysis.context: Thermodynamic formalism and ergodic properties of equilibrium states in non-uniform dynamics.

paper.title: Measure of Maximal Entropy for Geodesic Flows on Noncompact Manifolds of Nonpositive Curvature
paper.abstract: We establish the variational characterization of the measure of maximal entropy on noncompact manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature. Assuming that the deck transformation group contains an axial isometry with a rank-one axis and has a finite critical exponent, we prove that the supremum of the entropies of invariant probabilities equals the critical exponent and is attained if and only if the Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) measure is finite. In that case, the measure of maximal entropy is unique and equals the normalized BMS measure. The proof combines conditional-entropy rigidity on the regular set with an HTS-based entropy exclusion on the singular set, overcoming both non-compactness and the loss of uniform hyperbolicity due to zero curvature. We also obtain mixing under a non-arithmetic length-spectrum assumption. For nonpositively curved surfaces of genus at least two, the existence of a closed Jacobi rank-one geodesic and the non-arithmeticity of the axial length spectrum are automatic.

analysis.relevance_note: A variational characterization and uniqueness of maximal-entropy measures directly match entropy interests.
analysis.tldr: For noncompact manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature, the authors characterize attainment of the entropy supremum by finiteness of the BMS measure under rank-one and finite-critical-exponent assumptions.
analysis.problem: Characterize measures of maximal entropy for geodesic flows despite noncompactness and nonuniform hyperbolicity.
analysis.main_result: If the deck transformation group contains an axial isometry with a rank-one axis and has finite critical exponent, the supremum of invariant-probability entropies equals that exponent and is attained exactly when the Bowen–Margulis–Sullivan measure is finite. In that case the maximal-entropy measure is unique and is the normalized BMS measure. Mixing follows under a non-arithmetic length-spectrum assumption. For nonpositively curved surfaces of genus at least two, the abstract states that a closed Jacobi rank-one geodesic and non-arithmetic axial length spectrum are automatic.
methods: Conditional-entropy rigidity on the regular set.
HTS-based entropy exclusion on the singular set.
analysis.context: Entropy and invariant measures of nonpositively curved geodesic flows.

paper.title: Multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds and the optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials
paper.abstract: We establish uniform multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds for polynomials of Zakeri type, where all free critical points are on the boundary of an invariant Siegel disk of bounded type. This generalizes the unicritical result~\cite{DL:wZ}. As an application, we show the optimality of the Brjuno condition under the Zakeri restriction: as the rotation number becomes non-Brjuno, the Siegel disk evolves into the Cremer Hedgehog. Combined with~\cite{BCR26}, this implies the optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials, resolving a conjecture by Douady from the 1980s.

analysis.relevance_note: Siegel disks, critical boundaries and Cremer hedgehogs give a substantial complex-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: The authors establish multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds for Zakeri-type polynomials and derive optimality of the Brjuno condition under that restriction.
analysis.problem: Control invariant Siegel disks and determine optimality of the Brjuno condition for neutral polynomials.
analysis.main_result: Uniform multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds hold for Zakeri-type polynomials whose free critical points all lie on the boundary of an invariant bounded-type Siegel disk. The authors describe transition to a Cremer hedgehog as the rotation number becomes non-Brjuno. Combined with a cited result, they claim optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials, resolving the stated Douady conjecture.
methods: Uniform multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds; combination with a cited result whose details are not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Neutral polynomial dynamics and Siegel/Cremer behavior.

paper.title: The Assouad Dimension of Graphs: An Affirmative Answer to Fraser's Question
paper.abstract: This article primarily investigates the Assouad dimension of graphs of continuous functions. Initially, the Assouad spectrum of the graph of a H\"older and count-H\"older continuous function has been derived. It has been shown that the Assouad dimension of the graph of a continuous function $f:[a,b]\to \mathbb{R}$ with the count-H\"older condition is at least \( 1 + \sup \left\{ \overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}L_f(y) : y \in \mathscr{R}_f[a,b]\right\} \) where $\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}$ denotes the upper box dimension, $L_f(y)$ is the level set of $f$ at level $y$, and $\mathscr{R}_f[a,b]$ is the range of $f$ on $[a,b]$. As a consequence, non-trivial lower bounds are obtained for the Assouad dimension of the graphs of classical functions such as the Weierstrass and Takagi functions. We have also employed a unified projection solely in the direction of the $y$-axis to establish lower and upper bounds for the Assouad dimension. On this basis, we have shown that the lower bound is sharp in terms of level sets, namely the upper box dimension cannot be replaced by the Assouad dimension. This provides a partial positive answer to Question 17.11.1 posed by Fraser in~\cite{Fraser2021}, and to Question 2.2 posed by Yu in~\cite{Yu2020}. Building on this result, the analysis has been further extended to a broader class of Weierstrass-type functions and some self-affine functions like fractal interpolation functions. Moreover, we have discussed certain circumstances under which the Assouad dimension can reach 2 with several examples constructed. A supplementary explanation of why Brownian motion has the full Assouad dimension has also been provided based on the preceding work of Howroyd and Yu \cite{Howroyd2019}.

analysis.relevance_note: Assouad dimension and spectra of fractal graphs are central profile interests.
analysis.tldr: The authors obtain bounds and spectra for graphs of continuous functions and show sharpness of a lower bound using upper box dimensions of level sets.
analysis.problem: Relate Assouad dimension of a graph to regularity, projections and dimensions of its level sets.
analysis.main_result: For a continuous function satisfying the stated count-Hölder condition, graph Assouad dimension is at least one plus the supremum of upper box dimensions of its level sets over its range. The count-Hölder condition is not defined in the abstract. The upper box dimension cannot be replaced by Assouad dimension in this bound; despite the title, the abstract describes a partial positive answer to the cited questions. Applications include Weierstrass, Takagi, Weierstrass-type and fractal interpolation functions, with examples attaining dimension two.
methods: Projection in the direction of the vertical axis.
Construction of examples.
analysis.context: Assouad geometry of function graphs and fractal level sets.

paper.title: Minimal acceleration and the topology of premonotonic cocycles
paper.abstract: In his global theory of one-frequency Schr\"odinger operators~\cite{Av15}, Avila asked whether the acceleration of a real-analytic $\SL(2,\R)$ cocycle over an irrational circle rotation is bounded below by the absolute value of its topological degree and whether equality in nonzero degree characterizes premonotonicity. We answer this question affirmatively for every irrational frequency, without arithmetic restrictions. Here premonotonicity means that some iterate becomes strictly monotonic in the base variable after a periodic change of coordinates~\cite{AK15}. In the positive Lyapunov exponent regime, this provides a nonzero-degree counterpart to Avila's characterization of uniform hyperbolicity by vanishing acceleration. In nonzero degree, we also characterize minimal acceleration through signed connections and invariant positive matrix-valued measures. In the positive-degree, positive Lyapunov exponent case, the proof constructs an analytic positive connection using invariant positive matrix-valued measures and a transfer--scattering representation. A complex-analytic construction then produces a periodic gauge. As a further consequence, for each fixed irrational frequency and nonzero degree, the premonotonic locus is path connected: every cocycle in this locus can be joined to the linear rotation of the same degree by a path preserving premonotonicity.

analysis.relevance_note: Cocycle topology, invariant measures and uniform hyperbolicity provide substantial connections to the profile.
analysis.tldr: For real-analytic special-linear cocycles over irrational circle rotations, the authors prove the proposed acceleration lower bound and characterize equality in nonzero degree by premonotonicity.
analysis.problem: Relate acceleration to topological degree and describe the topology of the premonotonic locus.
analysis.main_result: For every irrational frequency, with no arithmetic restriction, acceleration is bounded below by absolute topological degree, with equality in nonzero degree characterizing premonotonicity. Here an iterate becomes strictly monotonic in the base after a periodic coordinate change. In nonzero degree, minimal acceleration is also characterized by signed connections and invariant positive matrix-valued measures; at fixed irrational frequency and nonzero degree, the premonotonic locus is path connected to the linear rotation of that degree through premonotonic cocycles.
methods: In the positive-degree, positive-Lyapunov-exponent case: analytic positive connections from invariant positive matrix-valued measures and a transfer–scattering representation.
A complex-analytic construction of a periodic gauge.
analysis.context: Analytic cocycles, acceleration, Lyapunov exponents and topology.

paper.title: Polynomial automorphisms of C^2 with the same equilibrium measure
paper.abstract: We review the following question: when do two polynomial automorphisms of C^2 have the same maximal entropy measure? While the answer has been known for some time when both automorphisms are compositions of H\'enon maps, the general case is more delicate. In this (mostly expository) note we explain how recent results in random dynamics give an almost complete solution to the question, and point out a number of related open problems.

analysis.relevance_note: Equality of maximal-entropy measures is a central entropy and equilibrium-measure question.
analysis.tldr: This mostly expository note reviews when two polynomial automorphisms of the complex plane squared share a maximal-entropy measure and explains an almost complete solution using recent random-dynamics results.
analysis.problem: Determine when two polynomial automorphisms have the same maximal-entropy measure, beyond the case of compositions of Hénon maps.
analysis.main_result: The abstract reports an almost complete solution based on recent random dynamics and identifies related open problems. The classification criteria and unresolved cases are not specified in the abstract.
methods: Recent results in random dynamics.
analysis.context: Complex polynomial automorphisms and maximal-entropy measures.

paper.title: Contact topology and intrinsic characterization of transversely vanishing curl eigenforms
paper.abstract: We study the geometry and topology of transversely vanishing eigenforms of the curl operator on $3$-manifolds, placing them in the broader framework of near-contact forms. We prove a Gray-type stability theorem for the kernels of near-contact forms, which we call near-contact structures, and derive a local neighborhood theorem around their singularities. As applications, we obtain a stability result for the contact topology of curl eigenforms, a classification of near-contact structures in terms of formal homotopical data, and a proof of the existence of contact structures on closed orientable 3-manifolds based on the spectral theory of the curl operator. We also study the symplectization of curl eigenforms as a possible bridge to symplectic dynamics. Finally, we characterize those transversely vanishing $1$-forms which are curl eigenforms for some smooth Riemannian metric. We deduce a generalization of the classical correspondence, due to Etnyre and Ghrist, between Reeb-like fields of contact forms and nowhere-vanishing rotational Beltrami fields to the setting of transversely vanishing vector fields.

analysis.relevance_note: Contact structures and the explicit link with symplectic dynamics provide a plausible geometric-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: The authors develop stability and local structure results for near-contact forms and characterize transversely vanishing curl eigenforms for some smooth Riemannian metric.
analysis.problem: Understand geometry, topology and intrinsic characterization of transversely vanishing curl eigenforms on three-manifolds.
analysis.main_result: The paper proves Gray-type stability for near-contact structures and a local neighborhood theorem around singularities. Applications include stability of contact topology for curl eigenforms, classification by formal homotopical data and existence of contact structures on closed orientable three-manifolds. It also extends the stated Reeb-like/rotational-Beltrami correspondence to transversely vanishing fields; symplectization is studied as a possible, rather than established, bridge to symplectic dynamics.
methods: Near-contact structures and their local neighborhood theorem.
Spectral theory of the curl operator.
Symplectization of curl eigenforms.
analysis.context: Contact topology, curl spectral geometry and possible connections to symplectic dynamics.

paper.title: Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control via Trajectory Optimization
paper.abstract: The curse of dimensionality associated with solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for the value function remains a key obstacle for real-time optimal feedback control of high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems. This is especially severe in aerospace applications such as relaminarizing unsteady turbulent flows and recovering from aerodynamic stall where nonlinear dynamics play a significant role. We introduce Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control (BASOC), a model reduction framework which seeks to find directions in state space along which the value function is most sensitive, and the distribution of states exhibits maximum variance along optimal trajectories. BASOC leverages trajectory optimization and the Pontryagin minimum principle to obtain state and co-state (value function gradient) data along locally optimal trajectories for constructing state and gradient covariance matrices. Balancing these matrices provides an oblique projection for approximating the value function, which can also be used to construct reduced-order models and surrogate feedback control laws. We show that for linear-quadratic optimal control problems, BASOC becomes equivalent to a snapshot method for initial condition balancing of the optimally controlled closed-loop realization. The framework is demonstrated on a nonlinear three-dimensional system where POD and balanced truncation are known to perform poorly, and on the nonlinear complex Ginzburg-Landau equation to demonstrate feasibility for larger-scale systems.

analysis.relevance_note: Model reduction for optimal feedback control is central, without a stated connection to the strongest research interests.

paper.title: Exact Generic Exponents of Approximation for the Action of the Integral Special Linear Group on the Torus
paper.abstract: Given an integer $n\ge 2$ and points $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$ lying in the $n$--dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^n$ equipped with its usual metric denoted by $\left\langle\;\cdot\;\right\rangle$, let \[ \tau_n(\mathbf x,\mathbf y) = \sup\left\{ \tau\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{there exist infinitely many } H\ge1\text{ for which}\\[1mm] \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-\tau} \text{ for some } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z) \end{array} \right\} \] be the Diophantine exponent of asymptotic approximation of $\mathbf{y}$ by the orbit of $\mathbf{x}$ under the action of the integral special linear group $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$. Let also \[ \widehat{\tau}_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right) = \sup\left\{ \tau\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{for all but finitely many } H\ge1, \text{ there is } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)\\[1mm] \text{such that } \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-\tau} \end{array} \right\} \] denote the corresponding exponent of uniform approximation. The main result of this paper proves that for almost all $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{T}^n$ (with respect to the induced Lebesgue measure), $$\widehat{\tau}_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; \tau_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; n-1.$$ This is the first result to establish the exact generic approximation exponents for an action of a lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)$ induced by the standard Euclidean action.

analysis.relevance_note: Diophantine exponents of a special-linear group action directly match group-action dynamics.
analysis.tldr: For the integral special-linear action on a torus of dimension at least two, the generic uniform and asymptotic approximation exponents both equal dimension minus one.
analysis.problem: Determine exact generic orbit-approximation exponents, with matrix norm bounded by a height parameter, for the integral special-linear action.
analysis.main_result: For every integer \(n\geq2\), the authors prove \(\widehat{\tau}_n(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})=\tau_n(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})=n-1\) for Lebesgue-almost every pair in \(\mathbb{T}^n\). The asymptotic exponent uses infinitely many heights, while the uniform exponent requires all sufficiently large heights. The abstract claims this as the first exact generic result for a lattice-subgroup action induced by the standard Euclidean action.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Homogeneous group actions and Diophantine approximation of torus orbits.

paper.title: Almost Periodicity Properties Arising From the Sodin-Yuditskii Theory
paper.abstract: The Kotani-Last problem and the Deift conjecture are two well known statements, which both concern the almost periodicity properties of the functions under consideration, and which have both been disproved in their original formulation, which involves Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity. To contrast these disproofs, and to further elucidate the essence of these two challenging problems, we establish positive results regarding each of them by showing that Weyl almost periodicity can be deduced whenever the Sodin-Yuditskii setup can be implemented. The latter requires that the Schr\"odinger operator associated with the function in question has purely absolutely continuous spectral measure and a spectrum with finite total gap length and the Parreau-Widom property. We also show that the known examples for which Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity has been shown or suggested to fail in the context of the Deift conjecture are in fact Weyl almost periodic. As a result, an accordingly modified version of the Deift conjecture remains a tantalizing open problem.

analysis.relevance_note: Almost periodicity supplies a plausible connection to recurrence and dynamical structure in spectral theory.
analysis.tldr: Within the Sodin–Yuditskii setup, the authors obtain Weyl almost periodicity in settings related to the Kotani–Last problem and Deift conjecture.
analysis.problem: Identify an almost-periodicity formulation compatible with counterexamples to the original Bohr/Bochner formulations.
analysis.main_result: Weyl almost periodicity follows whenever the Sodin–Yuditskii setup can be implemented, requiring the associated Schrödinger operator to have purely absolutely continuous spectral measure and spectrum of finite total gap length with the Parreau–Widom property. Known Deift-context examples where Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity fails or is suggested to fail are shown to be Weyl almost periodic. The accordingly modified Deift conjecture remains open.
methods: The Sodin–Yuditskii setup.
analysis.context: Almost periodicity and spectral theory of Schrödinger operators.

paper.title: Large deviations from a stable steady state for damped dispersive PDEs with vanishing random kicks
paper.abstract: We study the behaviour of stationary measures for a class of dispersive PDEs damped by a linear zero-order term and perturbed by a small kick noise. Under some natural assumptions on the law of the noise, we prove that any family of stationary measures satisfies the large deviation principle in the vanishing noise limit. The result highlights the role of nonlinear smoothing and applies to the nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Korteweg-de Vries equations, and to a variety of random perturbations including Gaussian and exponential variables.

analysis.relevance_note: Stationary measures and their large deviations give an invariant-measure connection despite the dispersive-PDE setting.
analysis.tldr: For linearly damped dispersive PDEs with small kick noise, the authors prove a large deviation principle for any family of stationary measures as the noise vanishes.
analysis.problem: Describe stationary-measure deviations from a stable steady state in the vanishing-noise limit.
analysis.main_result: The result holds under natural assumptions on the noise law, whose precise form is not specified in the abstract. Applications include nonlinear Schrödinger and Korteweg–de Vries equations and random perturbations including Gaussian and exponential variables.
methods: Nonlinear smoothing, whose role is highlighted in the abstract.
analysis.context: Stationary measures, large deviations and randomly perturbed dispersive PDEs.

paper.title: Exploring Neural Dynamics with Time Delays: A Numerical and Bifurcation Analysis Approach
paper.abstract: The Wilson-Cowan model is a classic example of a ``neural mass model'' - a simplified yet powerful way to describe the activity of large networks of neurons. It is particularly interesting because, even in its relatively simple form, it can produce a surprising variety of behaviours, from steady rhythms to complex oscillations. A key factor influencing these dynamics is the presence of time delays, reflecting the time it takes for signals to travel between neurons. This article offers an accessible introduction to the Wilson-Cowan model, focusing on how these time delays affect its behaviour. We explore the core concepts behind the model, survey the existing literature, and introduce some numerical techniques specifically designed for analysing such delay differential equations. We also provide a practical, hands-on tutorial on using the DDE-BIFTOOL software package, demonstrating its application to the Wilson-Cowan model. Downloadable code allows the reader to reproduce our results and to explore the model's dynamics further, including MATLAB code for all computations, using DDE-BIFTOOL for the continuation, and Python versions of simulation codes.

analysis.relevance_note: Numerical bifurcation and simulation of a delayed neural-mass model dominate the abstract, without a central profile connection.

paper.title: Stationary Coexistence in Stochastic Gause Systems with General Trophic Responses
paper.abstract: We study stationary coexistence in stochastic Gause predator-prey systems with independent multiplicative environmental noise and trophic responses depending on both population densities. A weighted population balance cancels the trophic interaction and yields moments of order greater than one without imposing predator self-regulation. These estimates give a direct occupation-measure proof of a sufficient coexistence criterion based on prey establishment and predator invasion of the prey-only stationary environment. For responses whose rare-predator limit is strictly increasing and whose value at positive predator density never exceeds that limit, we also establish necessity of positive predator invasion whenever the prey-only stationary law exists. If the prey per-capita growth attains its global maximum at zero, interior stationarity itself forces prey establishment, giving a necessary-and-sufficient criterion beyond logistic growth. Logistic and bounded saturating growth laws provide explicit Gamma and beta-prime resident distributions. Applications include Holling, Ivlev, Beddington-DeAngelis, and Crowley-Martin responses. Responses with the same rare-predator limit share the coexistence threshold, although predator interference changes the interior distribution. Reproducible quadrature and simulations illustrate this distinction. The analysis builds on existing stochastic persistence theory and identifies precisely the additional comparison argument needed for necessity, including exclusion of interior invariant measures at zero predator invasion.

analysis.relevance_note: Existence and exclusion of interior invariant measures give a plausible invariant-measure connection within stochastic ecological dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors establish stationary coexistence criteria for stochastic Gause predator–prey systems with independent multiplicative noise and general density-dependent trophic responses.
analysis.problem: Characterize interior stationarity using prey establishment and predator invasion, without imposing predator self-regulation.
analysis.main_result: Weighted population balance yields moments above order one and a sufficient coexistence criterion. If the rare-predator response limit is strictly increasing and bounds its value at positive predator density from above, positive predator invasion is necessary whenever the prey-only stationary law exists. If prey per-capita growth attains its global maximum at zero, interior stationarity forces prey establishment, giving a necessary-and-sufficient criterion beyond logistic growth under the stated setting. Responses with the same rare-predator limit share a threshold despite changes in interior distribution.
methods: Weighted population balance cancelling trophic interaction.
Occupation-measure proof and a comparison argument for necessity.
Quadrature and simulations for illustration.
analysis.context: Stochastic persistence and invariant measures in predator–prey systems.

paper.title: A semigroup approach for rough partial differential equations with jumps
paper.abstract: We establish an infinite-dimensional sewing lemma for discontinuous paths on a scale of Banach spaces. This allows us to construct Young and rough convolutions with jumps. Based on this we analyze the local and global well-posedness of semilinear parabolic rough partial differential equations (PDEs) with jumps in mixed space-time regularity spaces.

analysis.relevance_note: Well-posedness of rough parabolic PDEs with jumps is central, without a stated connection to the strongest profile themes.

paper.title: Escape of mass for finite-area hyperbolic surfaces
paper.abstract: Let $M$ be a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface. We give a lower bound for the $L^2$ norm of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series in a compact part of the surface. This extends a result of Soundararajan [arXiv:0901.4060] to the nonarithmetic setting. The crucial components of the proof are a long-time Egorov's theorem designed for this setting, a nonlinear uncertainty principle of Cohen--Dyatlov [arXiv:2609.30261], and an application of Weyl's method for exponential sums.

analysis.relevance_note: Escape of mass on hyperbolic surfaces connects to the geometric and invariant-measure side of dynamics.
analysis.tldr: On noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surfaces, the authors give a lower bound for the norm of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series in a compact region.
analysis.problem: Control escape of mass beyond the arithmetic setting.
analysis.main_result: The authors obtain a lower bound for the \(L^2\) norm in a compact part of a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface, extending a cited arithmetic result to the nonarithmetic setting. The quantitative bound is not specified in the abstract.
methods: A long-time Egorov theorem designed for this setting.
A cited nonlinear uncertainty principle.
Weyl’s method for exponential sums.
analysis.context: Hyperbolic spectral geometry and escape of mass.

paper.title: Silent Orbits and Cancellations in the Wave Trace
paper.abstract: This paper shows that the wave trace of a bounded and strictly convex planar domain may be arbitrarily smooth in a neighborhood of some point in the length spectrum. In other words, the Poisson relation, which asserts that the singular support of the wave trace is contained in the closure of $\pm$ the length spectrum, can almost be made into a strict inclusion. To do so, we construct large families of domains for which there exist multiple periodic billiard orbits having the same length but different Maslov indices. Using the microlocal Balian-Bloch-Zelditch parametrix for wave invariants developed in our previous paper, we solve a large system of equations for the boundary curvature jets, which leads to the required cancellations. We call such periodic orbits silent, since they are undetectable from the ostensibly audible wave trace. Such cancellations show that there are potential limitations in using the wave trace for inverse spectral problems and, more fundamentally, that the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum are inherently different mathematical objects, at least insofar as the wave trace is concerned.

analysis.relevance_note: Periodic billiard orbits and length spectra connect geometric dynamics with spectral questions.
analysis.tldr: The authors construct strictly convex bounded planar domains where cancellations make the wave trace arbitrarily smooth near some point of the length spectrum.
analysis.problem: Determine limitations of detecting periodic billiard orbits from wave-trace singularities.
analysis.main_result: Large families of domains have multiple periodic billiard orbits of equal length and different Maslov indices. Cancellations yield arbitrary smoothness near a length-spectrum point, so the Poisson relation can almost become a strict inclusion; the abstract does not assert a fully strict inclusion. These silent orbits demonstrate possible limitations of wave-trace inverse spectral methods.
methods: The microlocal Balian–Bloch–Zelditch parametrix for wave invariants from prior work.
Solving a large system for boundary curvature jets.
analysis.context: Periodic billiards, wave trace and inverse spectral geometry.

paper.title: NN-OpInf: an operator inference approach using structure-preserving composable neural networks
paper.abstract: We propose neural network operator inference (NN-OpInf): a structure-preserving, composable, and minimally restrictive operator inference framework for the non-intrusive reduced-order modeling of dynamical systems. The approach learns latent dynamics from snapshot data, enforcing local operator structure such as skew-symmetry, (semi-)positive definiteness, and gradient preservation, while also reflecting complex dynamics by supporting additive compositions of heterogeneous operators. We present practical training strategies and analyze computational costs relative to linear and quadratic polynomial OpInf (P-OpInf). Numerical experiments across several nonlinear and parametric problems demonstrate improved accuracy, stability, and robustness over P-OpInf and prior NN-ROM formulations, particularly when the dynamics are not well represented by polynomial models. These results suggest that NN-OpInf can serve as an effective drop-in replacement for P-OpInf when the dynamics to be modeled contain non-polynomial nonlinearities, offering potential gains in accuracy and out-of-distribution performance at the expense of higher training computational costs and a more difficult, non-convex learning problem.

analysis.relevance_note: Neural-network operator inference and reduced-order modeling are central, without the stated entropy, fractal or topological profile themes.

paper.title: On aggregation-quantization permutability problem for discrete-time Markov chains
paper.abstract: Given random walk on a graph, the corresponding discrete-time quantum walk can be constructed using the method proposed by Szegedy. On the other hand, given a partition of the set of states of a Markov chain, one can study the corresponding aggregated process. We extend the aggregation technique to the level of quantum Markov chains. We provide conditions under which application of these two operations - Szegedy's quantization and aggregation - give the same result. These consist of the strong lumpability of the underlying Markov chain supplemented by nonlinear relations, generalizing Kolmogorov's cycle condition, that account for the coefficients of both the original and the aggregated transition matrices. In particular, we show that the conditions are satisfied in the case of the random walk on graphs equipped with equitable partitions. We present several examples, which include the classical/quantum walks on Platonic solids. We discuss also relation of discrete-time classical/quantum walks on $N$-dimensional hypercube and the Ehrenfests urn model with $N$ particles. We apply our technique for of discrete-time walks on Cayley graphs of free groups. We also compare our results with those obtained using Cantero-Moral-Velazquez uniformization of unitary matrices.

analysis.relevance_note: Walks on Cayley graphs of free groups and aggregation of Markov dynamics provide a plausible connection, though group actions and entropy are not central.
analysis.tldr: The authors give conditions under which Szegedy quantization and aggregation of a discrete-time Markov chain commute.
analysis.problem: Extend aggregation to quantum Markov chains and determine compatibility with quantization.
analysis.main_result: The conditions consist of strong lumpability and nonlinear relations generalizing Kolmogorov’s cycle condition for original and aggregated transition matrices. They hold for random walks on graphs with equitable partitions. Examples include Platonic solids, hypercubes and the Ehrenfest urn model; the technique also applies to discrete-time walks on free-group Cayley graphs.
methods: Szegedy quantization and aggregation.
Strong lumpability with nonlinear cycle relations.
Comparison with Cantero–Moral–Velazquez uniformization.
analysis.context: Classical and quantum Markov walks and graph partitions.

paper.title: Structure-Aware Variational Learning of a Class of Generalized Diffusions
paper.abstract: Learning the underlying potential energy of stochastic gradient systems from partial and noisy observations is a fundamental problem arising in physics, chemistry, and data-driven modeling. Classical approaches often rely on direct regression of governing equations or velocity fields, which can be sensitive to noise and external perturbations and may fail when observations are incomplete. In this work, we propose a structure-aware, energy-based learning framework for inferring unknown potential functions in generalized diffusion processes, grounded in the energetic variational approach. Starting from the energy-dissipation law associated with the Fokker-Planck equation, we construct loss functions based on the De Giorgi dissipation functional, which consistently couple the free energy and the dissipation mechanism of the system. This formulation avoids explicit enforcement of the governing partial differential equation and preserves the underlying variational structure of the dynamics. Through numerical experiments in one, two, and three dimensions, we demonstrate that the proposed energy-based loss exhibits enhanced robustness with respect to observation time, noise level, and the diversity and amount of available training data. These results highlight the effectiveness of energy-dissipation principles as a reliable foundation for learning stochastic diffusion dynamics from data.

analysis.relevance_note: Energy-based learning of diffusion potentials is central; the variational terminology does not establish a thermodynamic-formalism connection.

paper.title: The Global Empirical NTK: Self-Referential Bias and Dimensionality of Gradient Descent Learning
paper.abstract: In training a neural network with gradient descent (GD), each iteration induces a linear operator that governs the first-order updates to a model's internal state variables. We call this operator the Global Empirical Neural Tangent Kernel (GeNTK). In finite-width networks, GeNTK is typically intractable to form, leading prior work to focus on restrictive settings, such as tracking only outputs or infinite-width limits. Here, we bridge this gap by studying the structure of GeNTK across many models. Formulating the model state as the solution to a global implicit constraint, we derive GeNTK as a product of two operators: K, accounting for immediate parameter-to-state interactions, and P, describing internal state-to-state dependencies. For a broad class of "weight-based models", such as RNNs and transformers, we prove a universal Kronecker-core theorem showing that K admits an exact, forward-pass-computable form given by the Gram matrix of weight-site variables. This core gives a measurable state-dependent restriction on Euclidean GD, termed "self-referential bias": current activity filters which adjoint directions can drive a first-order update. For recurrent models (GRUs and RNNs), we examine the spectrum of GeNTK and formalize notions of low-rank, biased learning in terms of reduced spatial or temporal ranks of the full operator. Practically, this explains why some RNN initializations yield better learning, while some plateau, by biasing the GeNTK and thus restricting learning to a small domain of learnable tasks. To demonstrate computational viability, we validate the main theorems in a self-attention transformer and a pretrained Pythia transformer language model with 410 million parameters. Overall, our results expose tractable local rank and mode-selective biases in the finite-width GD geometry and open the door to principled study of the GeNTK, a bridge between theory and practice.

analysis.relevance_note: Neural tangent kernels and rank restrictions of gradient-descent learning are central, rather than the specified dynamical dimension invariants.
